question: A histology slide shows a single cell layer composed of very thin, flattened cells with nuclei that bulge from the surface. Which epithelial class best matches this description?
cited_learning_objective: Visually and verbally classify (via number of cell layers, type of cell, and special features) surface epithelia and provide examples of locations of each class in the body.

options.rationale: Correct: A single layer of flattened cells with attenuated cytoplasm and bulging nuclei is characteristic of simple squamous epithelium; it appears as pavement or fried-egg shapes.
Wrong: Cuboidal cells are roughly equal in height and width; the described cells are flattened. It would be correct if cells were square in cross-section.
Wrong: Columnar cells are taller than wide with basally located nuclei; the slide shows attenuated, flattened cells. It would be correct if nuclei were elongated and basal.
Wrong: Stratified squamous has multiple layers with basal cuboidal cells; the specimen has a single layer. It would be correct if several cell layers were present.

Wrong: Pseudostratified appears crowded with nuclei at different levels though all cells contact the base; the cells here are uniformly flattened. It would be correct if nuclei were staggered at multiple levels.

question: Which epithelial type lines renal tubules and typically appears as a single layer of roughly square cells on cross-section?
cited_learning_objective: Visually and verbally classify (via number of cell layers, type of cell, and special features) surface epithelia and provide examples of locations of each class in the body.

options.rationale: Correct: Tubules of the kidney are lined by a single layer of cuboidal cells that appear square in cross-section and polygonal in surface view.
Wrong: Squamous cells are flattened and thin; renal tubule lining is not attenuated. It would be correct if the lining were a thin diffusion surface like endothelium.
Wrong: Columnar cells are taller than wide and line absorptive/secretory surfaces such as intestine, not renal tubules. It would be correct if cells were elongated with basal nuclei.
Wrong: Stratified squamous has multiple layers for protection; kidney tubules are single-layered. It would be correct if multiple protective layers were present.
Wrong: Transitional epithelium is specialized for stretch in the urinary tract; renal tubules are not lined by urothelium. It would be correct if the tissue were from bladder or ureter.

question: Which epithelial class is characterized by a single layer of tall cells with basally located nuclei and commonly lines secretory or absorptive surfaces?
cited_learning_objective: Visually and verbally classify (via number of cell layers, type of cell, and special features) surface epithelia and provide examples of locations of each class in the body.

options.rationale: Correct: Simple columnar epithelium consists of a single layer of rectangular cells with basally located nuclei and lines absorptive and secretory surfaces like stomach and intestine.
Wrong: Cuboidal cells are roughly equal in height and width; they do not have the tall columnar shape described. It would be correct if cells were square.
Wrong: Squamous cells are flattened and thin, not tall and columnar. It would be correct for diffusion surfaces like endothelium.
Wrong: Pseudostratified has nuclei at different levels though all cells contact the base; the description implies uniform single-layer columnar cells. It would be correct if nuclei were staggered.
Wrong: Stratified cuboidal has multiple layers and is not a single tall-cell layer; it would be correct if multiple cuboidal layers were present.

question: Which epithelial type is uniquely specialized to accommodate stretch and is limited to the urinary tract?
cited_learning_objective: Visually and verbally classify (via number of cell layers, type of cell, and special features) surface epithelia and provide examples of locations of each class in the body.

options.rationale: Correct: Transitional epithelium is a stratified epithelium specialized for stretch and found only in the urinary tract; surface cells change shape with distension.
Wrong: Stratified squamous is protective and found in skin and oral cavity, not specialized for stretch. It would be correct if the tissue required abrasion resistance rather than stretch.
Wrong: Pseudostratified is limited to the respiratory tract and is not specialized for urinary stretch. It would be correct if the sample were from airway mucosa.
Wrong: Simple columnar is single-layered and not designed for large changes in surface area; it would be correct for absorptive surfaces like intestine.
Wrong: Simple cuboidal is single-layered and lines ducts/tubules, not the distensible urinary tract. It would be correct for kidney tubules.

question: Which junctional complex links intermediate filaments of epithelial cells to the basement membrane and is targeted by autoantibodies in a blistering disease described in the slides?
cited_learning_objective: State the function of cellular junction types: desmosomes and hemidesmosomes.

options.rationale: Correct: Hemidesmosomes connect intermediate filaments to the basement membrane via integrins and laminins; anti-hemidesmosome antibodies cause subepidermal blistering as in bullous pemphigoid.
Wrong: Desmosomes link intermediate filaments between adjacent cells, not to the basement membrane; they would be implicated if cell-to-cell adhesion were disrupted.
Wrong: Tight junctions control paracellular diffusion and separate apical/basolateral membranes; they would be implicated if barrier permeability increased.
Wrong: The adhering belt links actin cytoskeletons of adjacent cells; it does not attach cells to the basement membrane. It would be correct if actin-based cell-cell cohesion failed.
Wrong: Gap junctions permit ion and small molecule passage between cells and do not anchor cells to the basement membrane; they would be implicated if intercellular signaling were lost.

question: A patient has a genetic defect in keratin intermediate filaments in epithelial cells. Which intercellular junction that connects to keratin filaments would most directly lose its mechanical strength?
cited_learning_objective: State the function of cellular junction types: desmosomes and hemidesmosomes.

options.rationale: Correct: Desmosomes connect intermediate filaments (keratins) between adjacent epithelial cells; defective keratin weakens cell-to-cell adhesion mediated by desmosomes.

Wrong: Hemidesmosomes link keratin to the basement membrane; while they also involve keratin, the question asks for intercellular junction between cells, which is desmosomes. It would be correct if the defect primarily affected cell-basement attachment.
Wrong: Tight junctions connect to actin, not keratin; keratin defects do not directly disrupt tight junctions. It would be correct if actin-associated proteins were mutated.
Wrong: The adhering belt links actin microfilaments between cells; keratin defects do not primarily affect this structure. It would be correct if actin-catenin-cadherin complexes were impaired.
Wrong: Gap junctions do not connect to intermediate filaments and are for small-molecule passage; keratin defects do not directly affect them. It would be correct if connexin proteins were mutated.

question: Which basement membrane component is produced by epithelial cells and forms the layer immediately adjacent to the basal plasma membrane?
cited_learning_objective: Visual identify and verbally describe the basement membrane.

options.rationale: Correct: The basal lamina is produced by epithelial cells and lies directly beneath the basal plasma membrane; together with the reticular lamina it forms the basement membrane.
Wrong: The reticular lamina is produced by connective tissue cells and lies beneath the basal lamina; it would be correct if the question asked about connective tissue-derived layer.
Wrong: 'Intercellular matrix' is not the specific epithelial-produced layer; the basal lamina is the precise term. It would be correct if the phrase specified epithelial-secreted basal layer.
Wrong: Glycocalyx is an apical cell-surface carbohydrate coat, not the basal lamina. It would be correct if the question targeted apical surface specializations.
Wrong: This is a nonspecific descriptor and does not identify the epithelial-produced basal lamina; it would be correct if connective tissue produced the layer immediately under epithelium.

question: A periodic acid–Schiff (PAS) stain highlights a continuous layer between epithelium and connective tissue. Which structure does this staining pattern identify?
cited_learning_objective: Visual identify and verbally describe the basement membrane.

options.rationale: Correct: The basement membrane (basal lamina plus reticular lamina) is PAS-positive and lies between epithelium and underlying connective tissue.
Wrong: Adventitia refers to connective tissue coverings of organs or vessels, not the PAS-positive epithelial basement membrane. It would be correct if describing outer connective coverings.
Wrong: Lamina propria is the subepithelial connective tissue, not the PAS-positive basement membrane itself. It would be correct if the connective tissue beneath the basement membrane were stained.

Wrong: PAS highlights the combined basement membrane (basal plus reticular lamina); naming only basal lamina is incomplete. It would be correct if the stain selectively highlighted epithelial-produced layer alone.

Wrong: Reticular lamina is connective tissue–derived and not the sole PAS-positive structure between epithelium and connective tissue. It would be correct if connective tissue components alone were stained.

question: Which apical specialization increases absorptive surface area and is described in the slides as aiding absorption in intestines and kidneys?
cited_learning_objective: Compare and contrast surface specializations: microvilli, stereocilia, and cilia.

options.rationale: Correct: Microvilli increase apical surface area to aid absorption in intestines and kidney tubules as described in the slides.
Wrong: Cilia are motile and involved in movement of fluids or cells, not primarily absorption. It would be correct if the function described was movement of mucus or ova.

Wrong: Stereocilia are long, nonmotile projections involved in absorption in male reproductive tract and sensory functions in the ear, not the primary absorptive microvilli of intestine. It would be correct if the site were epididymis or inner ear.

Wrong: Glycocalyx is a carbohydrate coat on the apical surface but is not the microvillus structure that increases surface area for absorption. It would be correct if the question targeted surface carbohydrate functions.
Wrong: Keratinized layers are protective and found in skin, not absorptive microvilli. It would be correct if the tissue were epidermis.

question: Which apical structure contains a 9+2 microtubule arrangement and depends on dynein arms for movement?
cited_learning_objective: Compare and contrast surface specializations: microvilli, stereocilia, and cilia.

options.rationale: Correct: Motile cilia have a 9 peripheral doublet plus 2 central microtubule arrangement and use dynein arms for movement.
Wrong: Microvilli are actin-based projections that increase surface area and do not have microtubule 9+2 structure or dynein-dependent motility. It would be correct if actin bundles were described.
Wrong: Stereocilia are long, actin-rich projections involved in absorption and sensory roles and lack the 9+2 microtubule axoneme. It would be correct if the structure were actin-based.

Wrong: Flagella (e.g., sperm tail) also have a 9+2 axoneme, but the slides specifically discuss apical epithelial specializations like cilia; flagellum is not an epithelial apical specialization. It would be correct if the question targeted sperm motility.
Wrong: Basal bodies nucleate cilia but are not the axonemal 9+2 structure itself; the axoneme (cilia) contains the 9+2 microtubules. It would be correct if the question asked about nucleation sites.

question: A patient with chronic sinusitis and infertility is found to have immotile respiratory cilia due to dynein arm defects. Which syndrome described in the slides best fits this presentation?
cited_learning_objective: Compare and contrast surface specializations: microvilli, stereocilia, and cilia.

options.rationale: Correct: Kartagener syndrome (a form of primary ciliary dyskinesia) features dynein arm defects causing chronic sinusitis, bronchiectasis, infertility, and sometimes situs inversus as noted in the slides.
Wrong: Bullous pemphigoid is an autoimmune blistering disease targeting hemidesmosomes, not a ciliary motility disorder. It would be correct if the presentation were subepidermal blistering.

Wrong: Cystic fibrosis causes thick secretions and recurrent sinopulmonary infections but is due to CFTR dysfunction, not dynein arm defects; infertility in CF is due to obstructive azoospermia. It would be correct if sweat chloride and CFTR mutation were present.
Wrong: Primary immunodeficiency can cause recurrent infections but does not explain ciliary immotility or situs inversus; it would be correct if immune cell defects were documented.

Wrong: A desmosome defect would cause cell-cell adhesion problems and blistering, not ciliary immotility; it would be correct if skin blistering and acantholysis were present. (Inference: combines two slide topics; not supported by slides.)

question: Which epithelial classification appears to have multiple layers on cross-section but actually consists of a single layer with all cells contacting the basement membrane?
cited_learning_objective: Visually and verbally classify (via number of cell layers, type of cell, and special features) surface epithelia and provide examples of locations of each class in the body.

options.rationale: Correct: Pseudostratified columnar epithelium appears stratified because nuclei are at different levels, but all cells contact the basement membrane; it is typical of the respiratory tract.
Wrong: Stratified squamous truly has multiple cell layers with only basal cells contacting the basement membrane; it would be correct if multiple layers were present.
Wrong: Simple columnar is a single uniform layer with basally located nuclei, not pseudostratified appearance. It would be correct if nuclei were aligned uniformly.
Wrong: Transitional epithelium is stratified and specialized for stretch, not a single layer contacting the basement membrane. It would be correct if surface cells changed shape with distension.
Wrong: Simple squamous is a single layer of flattened cells and does not show the crowded, staggered nuclei of pseudostratified epithelium. It would be correct if cells were attenuated and flat.

question: Which intercellular junction is located at the most apical portion of the lateral membrane, links to actin microfilaments, and prevents paracellular diffusion?
cited_learning_objective: State the function of cellular junction types: desmosomes and hemidesmosomes.

options.rationale: Correct: Tight junctions are at the luminal end of the lateral membrane, connect to actin microfilaments, and control paracellular diffusion and membrane domain separation.

Wrong: The adhering belt lies just deep to tight junctions and links actin between adjacent cells for cohesion, but tight junctions specifically prevent paracellular diffusion. It would be correct if the question asked about actin-based cell-cell linkage rather than barrier function.

Wrong: Desmosomes connect intermediate filaments between cells and provide mechanical strength, not paracellular barrier function. It would be correct if the question targeted keratin-linked adhesion.

Wrong: Hemidesmosomes anchor cells to the basement membrane via integrins and intermediate filaments, not to adjacent cells at the apical lateral membrane. It would be correct if the question asked about cell-basement attachment.
Wrong: Gap junctions allow passage of ions and small molecules between cells and do not form an apical diffusion barrier; it would be correct if intercellular signaling were the focus.

question: A biopsy shows separation just beneath the basal cell layer with intact desmosomes between keratinocytes. Autoantibodies are detected against proteins that bind the basement membrane. Which structure is the likely immunologic target?
cited_learning_objective: State the function of cellular junction types: desmosomes and hemidesmosomes.

options.rationale: Correct: Hemidesmosomes link basal keratinocytes to the basement membrane; antibodies against hemidesmosomal components cause subepidermal separation as in bullous pemphigoid described in the slides.
Wrong: Desmosomes mediate cell-to-cell adhesion; intact desmosomes would not explain subepidermal cleavage. It would be correct if intraepidermal acantholysis were present.
Wrong: Tight junction disruption would increase paracellular permeability but not cause subepidermal blistering; it would be correct if barrier leakage without cleavage were observed.
Wrong: The adhering belt links actin between adjacent cells and is not the primary anchor to the basement membrane; it would be correct if lateral actin-based cohesion failed.
Wrong: Gap junction antibodies would impair intercellular signaling but not cause mechanical separation at the basal layer; it would be correct if electrical coupling defects were documented.

question: Which epithelial surface specialization would you expect to find lining the respiratory tract and functioning to move mucus out of the airway?
cited_learning_objective: Compare and contrast surface specializations: microvilli, stereocilia, and cilia.

options.rationale: Correct: Respiratory epithelium is pseudostratified columnar and often ciliated; motile cilia move mucus and particulates out of the airway.
Wrong: Microvilli increase absorptive surface area and are typical of intestine and kidney, not mucus transport in airways. It would be correct if absorption were the function.
Wrong: Stereocilia are long, nonmotile projections found in male reproductive tract and inner ear, not on stratified squamous airway lining. It would be correct if the site were epididymis.
Wrong: Keratinization is protective and typical of skin epidermis, not mucus-moving respiratory epithelium. It would be correct if the tissue were external skin.
Wrong: Secretory apices produce mucus but do not provide the coordinated motility that cilia do; it would be correct if the question asked about mucus production rather than transport.

question: Which epithelial type is named according to the shape of the apical layer when multiple layers are present and often functions as a protective barrier?
cited_learning_objective: Visually and verbally classify (via number of cell layers, type of cell, and special features) surface epithelia and provide examples of locations of each class in the body.

options.rationale: Correct: Stratified epithelia are named for the apical layer; stratified squamous has multiple layers with squamous surface cells and serves a protective role in skin and mucosa.
Wrong: Simple epithelia are single-layered and not named for an apical layer in a multilayered context; it would be correct if only one flattened layer were present.

Wrong: Pseudostratified appears stratified but is actually simple; naming by apical layer in true stratified epithelia does not apply. It would be correct if all cells contacted the basement membrane.

Wrong: Transitional epithelium is stratified and specialized for stretch, but its apical cells change shape and are not simply described as squamous; it would be correct if the question emphasized stretch accommodation.
Wrong: Simple columnar is single-layered and not named for an apical layer in a multilayered epithelium; it would be correct if the tissue were a single tall-cell layer.

question: A researcher stains a tissue and observes a PAS-positive continuous band beneath epithelial cells. Which two layers combine to form this structure?
cited_learning_objective: Visual identify and verbally describe the basement membrane.

options.rationale: Correct: The basement membrane consists of the epithelial-produced basal lamina and the connective tissue–produced reticular lamina; together they are PAS-positive.
Wrong: Glycocalyx is an apical carbohydrate coat, not part of the basement membrane; it would be correct if the apical surface were being described.
Wrong: Lamina propria is subepithelial connective tissue, not a distinct layer of the basement membrane; it would be correct if the question asked about underlying connective tissue.
Wrong: Adventitia is a connective tissue covering of organs or vessels and is not the reticular lamina; it would be correct if describing outer organ coverings.
Wrong: Neither lamina propria nor glycocalyx constitute the PAS-positive basement membrane; it would be correct if both apical and connective tissue features were stained.

question: Which epithelial specialization is long, nonmotile, and functions in absorption in the male reproductive tract and sensory roles in the inner ear?
cited_learning_objective: Compare and contrast surface specializations: microvilli, stereocilia, and cilia.

options.rationale: Correct: Stereocilia are long, nonmotile, actin-rich projections involved in absorption in the male reproductive tract and sensory functions in the inner ear as noted in the slides.

Wrong: Microvilli are shorter actin-based projections that increase absorptive surface area in intestine and kidney, not the long stereocilia of epididymis or inner ear. It would be correct if the projections were short and densely packed.
Wrong: Motile cilia are microtubule-based and move fluids; they are not the long nonmotile stereocilia. It would be correct if coordinated movement were required.
Wrong: Keratin filaments are cytoskeletal intermediate filaments within cells, not apical projections; it would be correct if intracellular structural proteins were the focus.
Wrong: Basal bodies nucleate cilia but are not the long apical projections themselves; it would be correct if the question asked about ciliary nucleation.

question: Which junctional complex allows direct passage of ions and small molecules between adjacent epithelial cells and lacks cytoskeletal attachments?
cited_learning_objective: State the function of cellular junction types: desmosomes and hemidesmosomes.

options.rationale: Correct: Gap junctions, composed of connexins, permit passage of ions and small molecules between cells and do not attach to the cytoskeleton.
Wrong: Tight junctions control paracellular diffusion and attach to actin, not allow intercellular passage of small molecules. It would be correct if barrier function were the focus.
Wrong: Desmosomes provide mechanical linkage via intermediate filaments and do not permit ion passage; it would be correct if mechanical cohesion were impaired.
Wrong: Hemidesmosomes anchor cells to the basement membrane and are not channels for molecular passage; it would be correct if cell-basement attachment were disrupted.
Wrong: The adhering belt links actin between adjacent cells for cohesion and is not a conduit for ions or small molecules; it would be correct if actin-based adhesion were defective.

question: A pathologist notes that epithelial cells show a lateral membrane specialization immediately deep to tight junctions that links actin microfilaments between adjacent cells. What is this structure called?
cited_learning_objective: State the function of cellular junction types: desmosomes and hemidesmosomes.

options.rationale: Correct: The adhering belt (zonula adherens) lies just deep to tight junctions and links actin microfilaments between adjacent cells to form cohesive epithelium.

Wrong: Desmosomes connect intermediate filaments between cells and are not the actin-linked belt immediately deep to tight junctions. It would be correct if intermediate filament linkage were described.
Wrong: Tight junctions are at the luminal end and control paracellular diffusion; they are not the actin-linked adhering belt. It would be correct if barrier function were emphasized.
Wrong: Hemidesmosomes anchor cells to the basement membrane and involve intermediate filaments, not the lateral actin belt. It would be correct if cell-basement attachment were the focus.
Wrong: Gap junctions mediate intercellular signaling and do not link actin microfilaments between cells; it would be correct if ion passage were the feature.

question: Which epithelial type would you expect to find lining the gallbladder, based on its role in secretion and absorption and the slide examples?
cited_learning_objective: Visually and verbally classify (via number of cell layers, type of cell, and special features) surface epithelia and provide examples of locations of each class in the body.

options.rationale: Correct: The gallbladder is lined by simple columnar epithelium, a single layer of tall cells suited for secretion and absorption as listed in the slides.
Wrong: Simple cuboidal lines ducts and tubules like kidney tubules, not the gallbladder; it would be correct if the structure were a small duct.
Wrong: Pseudostratified is characteristic of the respiratory tract and not the gallbladder; it would be correct if the tissue were airway mucosa.
Wrong: Stratified squamous is protective and found in skin and oral mucosa, not in the gallbladder; it would be correct if abrasion protection were required.
Wrong: Transitional epithelium is limited to the urinary tract and accommodates stretch, not gallbladder function. It would be correct if the organ were bladder.

question: A slide of the epidermis shows keratinized surface cells and multiple underlying layers with cuboidal basal cells. Which epithelial classification does this represent?
cited_learning_objective: Visually and verbally classify (via number of cell layers, type of cell, and special features) surface epithelia and provide examples of locations of each class in the body.

options.rationale: Correct: The epidermis is keratinized stratified squamous epithelium with cuboidal basal cells and flattened keratinized surface cells, serving a protective function.
Wrong: Simple squamous is a single thin layer and does not form the multi-layered keratinized epidermis; it would be correct for endothelium or mesothelium.
Wrong: Simple columnar is single-layered and not keratinized; it would be correct for intestinal lining.
Wrong: Pseudostratified appears stratified but is single-layered and is found in the respiratory tract, not keratinized epidermis. It would be correct if nuclei were staggered.
Wrong: Transitional epithelium is specialized for stretch in the urinary tract and is not keratinized; it would be correct if the tissue were bladder.

question: Which epithelial feature prevents exchange of intrinsic proteins and lipids between apical and basolateral plasma membrane domains?
cited_learning_objective: State the function of cellular junction types: desmosomes and hemidesmosomes.

options.rationale: Correct: Tight junctions prevent mixing of apical and basolateral membrane components and control paracellular diffusion, maintaining membrane polarity.
Wrong: Desmosomes provide mechanical linkage between cells via intermediate filaments but do not maintain membrane domain separation. It would be correct if mechanical cohesion were the focus.

Wrong: Hemidesmosomes anchor cells to the basement membrane and do not prevent membrane protein diffusion between apical and basolateral domains. It would be correct if cell-basement attachment were disrupted.
Wrong: Gap junctions allow passage of small molecules between cells and do not separate membrane domains. It would be correct if intercellular signaling were the question.
Wrong: The adhering belt links actin cytoskeletons for cohesion but does not prevent membrane protein exchange between domains. It would be correct if actin-based adhesion were impaired.

question: A male patient has infertility due to impaired absorption in the epididymis. Which apical specialization described in the slides is most likely dysfunctional?
cited_learning_objective: Compare and contrast surface specializations: microvilli, stereocilia, and cilia.

options.rationale: Correct: Stereocilia are long, nonmotile projections that aid absorption in the male reproductive tract (epididymis); dysfunction would impair luminal fluid absorption and sperm maturation.

Wrong: Motile cilia move fluids and are important in airways and reproductive tract transport but are not the primary absorptive projections in the epididymis. It would be correct if transport of sperm along the tract were defective.

Wrong: Microvilli increase absorptive area in intestine and kidney but are shorter than stereocilia and not the main epididymal specialization. It would be correct if the absorptive surface were densely packed short projections.

Wrong: Basal infoldings increase membrane area for ion transport in some epithelia but are not the apical stereocilia of the epididymis. It would be correct if ion transport across the basal membrane were implicated.
Wrong: Keratinization is protective and not involved in epididymal absorption; it would be correct if the tissue were epidermis.

question: During tissue processing, a student notes that the epithelial basement membrane appears as two layers: one produced by epithelial cells and one by connective tissue. Which pair correctly names these layers?
cited_learning_objective: Visual identify and verbally describe the basement membrane.

options.rationale: Correct: The basal lamina is produced by epithelial cells and the reticular lamina by connective tissue; together they form the basement membrane.
Wrong: Lamina propria is the subepithelial connective tissue, not the reticular lamina specifically; it would be correct if the question asked about underlying connective tissue broadly.
Wrong: Adventitia is an outer connective tissue covering and not the epithelial-produced basal lamina; it would be correct if describing organ coverings.
Wrong: Glycocalyx is an apical carbohydrate coat, not a connective tissue–derived layer beneath epithelium. It would be correct if apical surface features were being described.
Wrong: These are deeper layers of mucosa and not the two-layered basement membrane; it would be correct if the question targeted mucosal architecture rather than the basement membrane.

question: A histologist wants to identify epithelial cells using immunohistochemistry for cytoskeletal intermediate filaments produced by epithelia. Which marker family mentioned in the slides should they target?
cited_learning_objective: Visually and verbally classify (via number of cell layers, type of cell, and special features) surface epithelia and provide examples of locations of each class in the body.

options.rationale: Correct: Epithelial cells produce cytokeratin intermediate filaments, which serve as useful immunohistochemical markers for epithelial-derived tumors.
Wrong: Vimentin is an intermediate filament of mesenchymal cells, not epithelial cytokeratins; it would be correct if the cells were connective tissue–derived.
Wrong: Desmin is a muscle-specific intermediate filament and not an epithelial marker; it would be correct if the tissue were muscle.
Wrong: Neurofilament proteins are neuronal intermediate filaments, not epithelial cytokeratins; it would be correct if neuronal tissue were being identified.
Wrong: GFAP is an intermediate filament in glial cells and not an epithelial marker; it would be correct if glial cells were the target.

question: A patient presents with subepidermal blisters and antibodies against proteins that bind laminin in the basement membrane. Which clinical finding from the slides best explains the level of cleavage seen on histology?
cited_learning_objective: State the function of cellular junction types: desmosomes and hemidesmosomes.

options.text: Autoantibodies to hemidesmosomes causing separation under basal cells
options.rationale: Correct: Hemidesmosomes anchor basal cells to the basement membrane; antibodies against hemidesmosomal components produce subepidermal cleavage as in bullous pemphigoid described in the slides.

options.text: Autoantibodies to desmoglein causing intraepidermal acantholysis
options.rationale: Wrong: Desmoglein antibodies (pemphigus vulgaris) cause intraepidermal blistering due to desmosome disruption, not subepidermal separation. It would be correct if histology showed suprabasal cleavage.

options.text: Loss of tight junctions causing epidermal sloughing
options.rationale: Wrong: Tight junction loss increases permeability but does not produce the mechanical subepidermal blistering seen with hemidesmosome antibodies. It would be correct if barrier dysfunction without cleavage were observed.

options.text: Basal cell apoptosis leading to epidermal detachment
options.rationale: Wrong: Apoptosis of basal cells could cause detachment but the slides specifically link hemidesmosome antibodies to subepidermal blisters; it would be correct if apoptosis were documented.

options.text: Autoimmune targeting of gap junctions causing blistering
options.rationale: Wrong: Gap junction targeting would impair intercellular signaling but would not directly cause subepidermal blister formation; it would be correct if electrical coupling defects led to tissue breakdown.

question: Which epithelial type is correctly paired with a slide example location: lining of blood and lymphatic vessels?
cited_learning_objective: Visually and verbally classify (via number of cell layers, type of cell, and special features) surface epithelia and provide examples of locations of each class in the body.

options.rationale: Correct: Endothelium is a simple squamous epithelium lining blood and lymphatic vessels, matching the slide example.
Wrong: Endothelium is squamous, not cuboidal; it would be correct if vessel lining cells were square in cross-section, which they are not.
Wrong: Endothelium is single-layered; stratified squamous is multilayered and protective, not vascular lining. It would be correct if multiple layers lined the vessel.
Wrong: Pseudostratified columnar is respiratory epithelium and not the vascular endothelium. It would be correct if the tissue were airway mucosa.
Wrong: Transitional epithelium is urinary tract–specific and not vascular endothelium. It would be correct if the tissue were bladder.

question: Which apical specialization would be most affected by a mutation that disrupts actin microfilament bundles within apical projections?
cited_learning_objective: Compare and contrast surface specializations: microvilli, stereocilia, and cilia.

options.rationale: Correct: Both microvilli and stereocilia are actin-based apical projections; disruption of actin bundles would impair their structure and absorptive/sensory functions.
Wrong: Motile cilia are microtubule-based (9+2 axoneme) and depend on dynein, not actin; it would be correct if microtubule-associated proteins were disrupted.
Wrong: Basal bodies nucleate cilia and are microtubule-related structures; actin disruption would not primarily affect basal bodies. It would be correct if basal body formation were impaired.
Wrong: Keratinized layers are composed of intermediate filaments and keratin, not apical actin bundles; it would be correct if keratin synthesis were defective.

Wrong: Not all apical specializations are actin-based; cilia are microtubule-based, so actin disruption would not equally affect them. It would be correct only if both actin and microtubules were disrupted.

question: A surgical specimen from the esophagus shows a nonkeratinized, multilayered epithelium with surface flattened cells. Which epithelial classification and primary function best match this finding?
cited_learning_objective: Visually and verbally classify (via number of cell layers, type of cell, and special features) surface epithelia and provide examples of locations of each class in the body.

options.rationale: Correct: The esophagus is lined by nonkeratinized stratified squamous epithelium; multiple layers and flattened surface cells provide protection against abrasion.

Wrong: Simple columnar is single-layered and suited for secretion/absorption (stomach, intestine), not the protective multilayered esophageal lining. It would be correct if the tissue were gastric mucosa.

options.text: Pseudostratified columnar epithelium for mucociliary clearance
options.rationale: Wrong: Pseudostratified ciliated epithelium is respiratory and not the esophageal lining; it would be correct if the specimen were from the trachea.
Wrong: Transitional epithelium accommodates stretch in the urinary tract and is not found in the esophagus; it would be correct if the organ were bladder.
Wrong: Simple squamous is thin for diffusion (endothelium/mesothelium) and not protective multilayered epithelium; it would be correct if the tissue were vascular lining.

question: Which epithelial type lines body cavities such as the pleura and peritoneum and is mentioned in the slides as an example?
cited_learning_objective: Visually and verbally classify (via number of cell layers, type of cell, and special features) surface epithelia and provide examples of locations of each class in the body.

options.rationale: Correct: Mesothelium is a simple squamous epithelium that lines body cavities like pleura and peritoneum, as noted in the slides.
Wrong: Endothelium is simple squamous, not cuboidal, and lines blood vessels; the pairing is incorrect. It would be correct if endothelium were described as squamous.
Wrong: Mesothelium is simple squamous, not pseudostratified columnar; it would be correct if the lining were respiratory mucosa.
Wrong: Mesothelium is single-layered and squamous, not stratified cuboidal; it would be correct if multiple cuboidal layers lined the cavity.
Wrong: Transitional epithelium is urinary tract–specific and not mesothelium; it would be correct if the tissue were bladder.

question: Which epithelial junction's main protein components include claudins and occludins and is essential for maintaining distinct apical and basolateral membrane domains?
cited_learning_objective: State the function of cellular junction types: desmosomes and hemidesmosomes.

options.rationale: Correct: Tight junctions are composed of claudins and occludins and prevent exchange of proteins and lipids between apical and basolateral membranes, maintaining polarity.
Wrong: Desmosomes are cadherin-based and link intermediate filaments between cells, not claudins/occludins; it would be correct if intermediate filament linkage were described.
Wrong: The adhering belt involves cadherins and catenins linking actin, not claudins/occludins; it would be correct if actin linkage were the focus.
Wrong: Hemidesmosomes use integrins and laminins to attach cells to the basement membrane, not claudins/occludins; it would be correct if cell-basement anchoring were asked.
Wrong: Gap junctions are connexin-based channels for small molecules and ions, not claudins/occludins; it would be correct if intercellular communication were the focus.

question: A pathology slide shows epithelial cells with intermediate filament bundles connected to lateral plaques between cells. Which junction is being visualized?
cited_learning_objective: State the function of cellular junction types: desmosomes and hemidesmosomes.

options.rationale: Correct: Desmosomes link intermediate filaments (keratins) between adjacent cells via cadherins and appear as lateral plaques connecting cytoskeletons.
Wrong: Hemidesmosomes anchor intermediate filaments to the basement membrane rather than between adjacent cells; it would be correct if cell-basement attachment were shown.
Wrong: Tight junctions are apical and link to actin, not intermediate filaments; it would be correct if barrier function were visualized.
Wrong: The adhering belt links actin microfilaments between cells and is not associated with intermediate filament plaques; it would be correct if actin bundles were seen.
Wrong: Gap junctions are channels for ions and small molecules and lack cytoskeletal attachments; it would be correct if intercellular communication structures were observed.

question: Which epithelial classification is limited to the respiratory tract and may be ciliated, as noted in the slides?
cited_learning_objective: Visually and verbally classify (via number of cell layers, type of cell, and special features) surface epithelia and provide examples of locations of each class in the body.

options.rationale: Correct: Pseudostratified columnar epithelium, often ciliated, is characteristic of the respiratory tract and appears crowded with nuclei at different levels.
Wrong: Simple columnar is single-layered and lines digestive tract and gallbladder, not specifically the respiratory tract; it would be correct if the tissue were intestine.
Wrong: Stratified squamous is protective and found in skin and oral cavity, not the typical respiratory lining; it would be correct if abrasion protection were needed.
Wrong: Simple cuboidal lines ducts and tubules like kidney, not the respiratory tract; it would be correct if the sample were a duct.
Wrong: Transitional epithelium is urinary tract–specific and not respiratory; it would be correct if the tissue were bladder.

question: A clinician examines a mucosal biopsy and notes a cobblestone apical surface with dome-shaped superficial cells when the organ is relaxed, and flattening when distended. Which epithelium is this?
cited_learning_objective: Visually and verbally classify (via number of cell layers, type of cell, and special features) surface epithelia and provide examples of locations of each class in the body.

options.rationale: Correct: Transitional epithelium has dome or umbrella cells that appear puffy when non-distended and flatten when distended, and is limited to the urinary tract.
Wrong: Stratified squamous does not show dome-shaped umbrella cells that flatten with stretch; it would be correct if the surface were protective and non-distensible.
Wrong: Pseudostratified has staggered nuclei and cilia in respiratory tract, not dome-shaped umbrella cells; it would be correct if nuclei were at multiple levels.
Wrong: Simple columnar is single-layered and does not exhibit the stretch-related dome-to-flat transition; it would be correct if the tissue were absorptive.
Wrong: Simple cuboidal is single-layered and square in cross-section, not cobblestone dome-surfaced; it would be correct if lining small ducts.

question: Which epithelial surface specialization is primarily responsible for moving ova in the female reproductive tract and cerebrospinal fluid in brain ventricles, according to the slides?
cited_learning_objective: Compare and contrast surface specializations: microvilli, stereocilia, and cilia.

options.rationale: Correct: Motile cilia move fluids and cells, functioning in airways, female reproductive tract (ova transport), and brain ventricular lining as described in the slides.
Wrong: Microvilli increase absorptive surface area and do not provide coordinated movement of fluids; it would be correct if absorption were the required function.
Wrong: Stereocilia are nonmotile and involved in absorption and sensory roles, not bulk fluid movement; it would be correct if sensory transduction were the function.
Wrong: Basal infoldings increase membrane area for transport but do not move fluids along the lumen; it would be correct if ion transport across the basal membrane were implicated.
Wrong: Glycocalyx is a carbohydrate coat and does not generate coordinated movement of fluids; it would be correct if surface protection or enzyme localization were the focus.

question: A student confuses desmosomes and hemidesmosomes. Which concise contrast from the slides correctly distinguishes their primary attachments?
cited_learning_objective: State the function of cellular junction types: desmosomes and hemidesmosomes.

options.text: Desmosomes link cells to cells; hemidesmosomes link cells to basement membrane
options.rationale: Correct: Desmosomes connect intermediate filaments between adjacent cells for cell-to-cell adhesion, while hemidesmosomes anchor cells to the basement membrane.

options.text: Desmosomes link cells to basement membrane; hemidesmosomes link cells to cells
options.rationale: Wrong: This reverses the actual attachments; it would be correct only if the terms were swapped.

options.text: Both link cells to basement membrane
options.rationale: Wrong: Only hemidesmosomes link to the basement membrane; desmosomes connect adjacent cells. It would be correct if both structures attached to the basal lamina.

options.text: Both link cells to cells via actin
options.rationale: Wrong: Desmosomes link via intermediate filaments, not actin, and hemidesmosomes link to basement membrane; it would be correct if actin were the cytoskeletal connection for both.

options.text: Desmosomes are gap junctions; hemidesmosomes are tight junctions
options.rationale: Wrong: This confuses distinct junction types and functions; desmosomes are adhesive plaques and hemidesmosomes anchor to basement membrane. It would be correct only if nomenclature were entirely different.

question: Which epithelial type would you expect to find lining the oral cavity and esophagus where protection from abrasion is required?
cited_learning_objective: Visually and verbally classify (via number of cell layers, type of cell, and special features) surface epithelia and provide examples of locations of each class in the body.

options.rationale: Correct: The oral cavity and esophagus are lined by stratified squamous epithelium, which provides protection against abrasion.
Wrong: Simple columnar is single-layered and suited for secretion/absorption, not abrasion protection; it would be correct for intestinal lining.
Wrong: Pseudostratified ciliated epithelium is respiratory and not typical of oral cavity or esophagus; it would be correct if the tissue were airway mucosa.
Wrong: Simple cuboidal lines ducts and tubules and is not protective multilayered epithelium; it would be correct if the tissue were a small duct.
Wrong: Transitional epithelium is urinary tract–specific and not found in oral cavity or esophagus; it would be correct if the organ were bladder.

question: A researcher examines an epithelial tumor and uses cytokeratin immunostaining to confirm epithelial origin. Why is cytokeratin a suitable marker based on the slides?
cited_learning_objective: Visually and verbally classify (via number of cell layers, type of cell, and special features) surface epithelia and provide examples of locations of each class in the body.

options.text: Epithelial cells produce cytokeratin intermediate filaments
options.rationale: Correct: Epithelial cells synthesize cytokeratin intermediate filaments as part of their cytoskeleton, making cytokeratin a reliable epithelial marker.

options.text: Cytokeratin is unique to connective tissue
options.rationale: Wrong: Cytokeratin is not a connective tissue marker; vimentin is typical for mesenchymal cells. It would be correct only if connective tissue cells produced cytokeratin.
Wrong: Cytokeratin marks intracellular intermediate filaments in epithelial cells, not the extracellular basement membrane; it would be correct if the stain targeted extracellular matrix.
Wrong: Cilia are microtubule-based structures and are not identified by cytokeratin; it would be correct if the marker targeted microtubule proteins.

options.text: Cytokeratin is specific for neuronal tissue
options.rationale: Wrong: Neuronal intermediate filaments are neurofilaments, not cytokeratins; it would be correct if neuronal markers were being used.

question: Which epithelial specialization would be least affected by a defect in dynein motor proteins?
cited_learning_objective: Compare and contrast surface specializations: microvilli, stereocilia, and cilia.

options.rationale: Correct: Microvilli are actin-based and do not rely on dynein motors; dynein defects primarily impair motile cilia which are microtubule-based.
Wrong: Motile cilia depend on dynein arms for movement and would be severely affected by dynein defects. It would be correct only if dynein were intact.
Wrong: Stereocilia are actin-based and nonmotile, so they are not dynein-dependent; they would be affected only by actin-related defects. It would be correct if actin bundles were disrupted.
Wrong: Basal bodies nucleate cilia and while dynein defects impair ciliary motility, basal bodies themselves are not motor proteins; it would be correct if basal body formation were defective.
Wrong: Gap junctions mediate intercellular communication and are unrelated to dynein motor function; it would be correct if intercellular signaling were the issue.

question: A patient with situs inversus, chronic sinusitis, and bronchiectasis is suspected to have a defect in which cellular structure described in the slides?
cited_learning_objective: Compare and contrast surface specializations: microvilli, stereocilia, and cilia.

options.text: Axonemal dynein arms of motile cilia
options.rationale: Correct: Defects in axonemal dynein arms impair motile cilia function causing primary ciliary dyskinesia (Kartagener syndrome) with situs inversus, chronic sinusitis, and bronchiectasis.
Wrong: Actin bundle defects affect microvilli and absorption, not situs inversus or bronchiectasis; it would be correct if malabsorption were present.
Wrong: Desmosomal intermediate filament defects cause adhesion problems and blistering, not ciliary motility disorders; it would be correct if skin blistering occurred.
Wrong: Hemidesmosome defects cause subepidermal blistering like bullous pemphigoid, not situs inversus or bronchiectasis; it would be correct if subepidermal blisters were present.
Wrong: Connexin defects impair intercellular signaling and are not linked to situs inversus or chronic sinusitis; it would be correct if electrical coupling defects were documented.

question: Which epithelial classification is correctly matched with its primary slide example location: epidermis, oral cavity, esophagus, cervix, and vagina?
cited_learning_objective: Visually and verbally classify (via number of cell layers, type of cell, and special features) surface epithelia and provide examples of locations of each class in the body.

options.rationale: Correct: These mucosal and cutaneous surfaces are lined by stratified squamous epithelium, which may be keratinized (skin) or nonkeratinized (oral cavity, esophagus, cervix, vagina) as noted in the slides.
Wrong: Simple columnar lines stomach and intestine, not the multilayered protective surfaces listed; it would be correct if the tissue were gastrointestinal mucosa.
Wrong: Pseudostratified is respiratory and not typical of the listed sites; it would be correct if the tissue were trachea.
Wrong: Simple cuboidal lines ducts and tubules like kidney, not the protective stratified surfaces listed; it would be correct if the sample were renal tubules.
Wrong: Transitional epithelium is urinary tract–specific and not found in the listed reproductive and alimentary sites; it would be correct if the organ were bladder.
